summary: Late and missing WhatsApp replies come from the outbound path. msg-delivery workers are running out of memory and being killed repeatedly, so outbound-msgs consumers fell from 4 to 2 and its depth grew steadily from about 08:55 to 1281 by 09:30. msg-delivery memory started climbing right after deploy msg-delivery-00277 (08:49, 'batch size increase for delivery receipts'). That deploy is the likely trigger, but I have no direct proof of how it causes the memory growth. inbound-msgs and portfolio-updates are healthy, and the orchestrator and aa-sync deploys do not fit the timing or the symptoms. Unrelated services were not checked in detail.

hypotheses.statement: msg-delivery is OOM-killed with a memory leak or oversized batches, likely introduced by deploy msg-delivery-00277. Consumer capacity on outbound-msgs halves and the backlog grows, so replies are delayed.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: msg-delivery deploy with a batch size increase landed at 08:49, just before the memory climb
msg-delivery memory pressure began right after the deploy and climbed steadily
msg-delivery workers began being OOM-killed at 09:05
Messages were redelivered on outbound-msgs after the kills
outbound-msgs consumers dropped from 4 to 2 and stayed there
outbound-msgs depth started rising at 08:55, before the consumer count dropped, then grew steadily
msg-delivery memory peaked at the 99% limit and workers restarted up to 5 times in 5 minutes
msg-delivery consumes only from outbound-msgs, so its failure directly backs up that queue
The larger batch size in msg-delivery-00277 probably causes the memory growth, for example by holding more receipts in memory per batch. This is inferred from timing only.

hypotheses.statement: The backlog comes from upstream load or another service (orchestrator or inbound path) rather than from msg-delivery.
hypotheses.label: low

contradicting.text: The inbound queue is healthy, so the problem is not upstream of the outbound queue

unresolved: Whether the batch size change in msg-delivery-00277 is the actual cause of the memory growth. The evidence is timing only, and a rollback would test it.
The msg-delivery logs were truncated at 09:08. Later behaviour and any other error types were not reviewed.
Why some replies never arrive. The DLQ is 0, so loss may come from OOM kills mid-processing or from expiry, and this was not verified.
Config changes and WhatsApp-side delivery receipts were not examined. Orchestrator, llm-gateway and the other services were not checked individually.

actions.text: Roll back msg-delivery-00277, or revert the delivery-receipt batch size, and restart the msg-delivery workers.
actions.rationale: The memory climb starts right after this deploy and drives the OOM kills that halve consumer capacity.

actions.text: Temporarily scale out msg-delivery consumers on outbound-msgs and raise the memory limit while the rollback proceeds. Watch depth and redeliveries until the backlog drains.
actions.rationale: Depth is still growing at about 200 per 5 minutes with only 2 consumers.

actions.text: Profile msg-delivery memory with the new batch size and check whether redelivered messages are duplicated or lost for users.
actions.rationale: OOM kills cause redeliveries, and the report says some replies never arrive.
